examples: An egg is fragile. Do not drop it!
The fragile cup broke.
Baby birds are fragile.

more.def: Easily broken, so it must be handled with care.
examples: The box was marked "fragile" because it held glass cups.
The old book's pages were thin and fragile.
Carry the model carefully because it is fragile.

easy.def: A border that goes around a picture or a window.
examples: The picture is in a frame.
The frame is gold.
The window frame is wood.

more.def: A border or case that holds a picture, mirror or window, or the main structure of something.
examples: She put the photo in a wooden frame.
The window frame was painted white.
The frame of the bike is made of metal.
Borrowing books at the library is free.
I got a free ticket.
We got a free sample of cheese.

more.def: Not costing anything; given without payment.
examples: The museum has free tickets for children on Sundays.
Everyone at the school fair got a free balloon.
Water from the fountain is free.
The bird flew away, free at last.
After the cage opened, the rabbit was free.
Let the dog run free.

more.def: Not held, tied or locked up; able to move or act as you like.
examples: The kitten was finally free of the tangled yarn.
People in a free country can say what they think.
Once the gate opened, the horses were free to run across the field.
Are you free on Saturday?
I am free after lunch.
The bathroom is free now.

more.def: Not busy, so there is time to do something.
examples: Are you free to play after school today?
Dad will be free after he finishes his work.
I have a free hour before dinner.

easy.def: To let someone or something go.
examples: We freed the butterfly.
The farmer freed the lamb from the fence.
Mom freed my kite from the tree.

more.def: To let a person or animal go from something that holds them.
examples: The rescuers freed the whale from the fishing net.
The gardener freed the vine from the tangled wire.
She freed the puppy from its leash at the park.

easy.def: Being able to do and say what you want.
examples: The bird flew away to freedom.
The dog loves the freedom of the big yard.
We have the freedom to pick our own books.

more.def: The right to act, speak, and think as you choose.
examples: The people fought for their freedom.
Summer vacation gives kids the freedom to play all day.
The zoo released the healed eagle back to freedom.
Water freezes in the cold.
The pond froze.
The juice froze in the freezer.

more.def: To become hard as ice when it is very cold.
examples: Water freezes when the temperature drops.
The pond froze solid last night.
We put the berries in the freezer to freeze them.
Freeze!
The deer froze.
The kids froze when the music stopped.

more.def: To stop moving suddenly.
examples: The deer froze when it heard a noise.
The players froze when the whistle blew.
The rabbit froze in the grass.
The bread is fresh.
Put on fresh socks.
Fresh flowers are in the vase.

more.def: Newly made, picked or cleaned, and not old or stale.
examples: The bakery sells fresh bread every morning.
We picked fresh strawberries from the garden.
She opened the window for fresh air.
Rivers have fresh water.
The lake has fresh water.
Fish live in fresh water.

more.def: Not salty, used about water.
examples: Most lakes have fresh water.
Salmon swim from the sea into fresh water.
Fresh water is needed for drinking.

easy.def: The last school day of the week.
examples: Friday is pizza day.
We have a spelling test on Friday.
Dad gets home early on Friday.

more.def: The day of the week that comes after Thursday and before Saturday.
examples: Friday is the last day of school before the weekend.
We watch a movie in class on Friday afternoon.
She was born on a Friday in June.

easy.def: A person you like and who likes you.
examples: She is my friend.
I play with my friends.
My dog is my best friend.

more.def: A person you know well and like, and who likes you too.
examples: My best friend and I walk to school together every day.
A good friend listens when you feel sad.
He made a new friend on the first day of camp.
The new girl is friendly.
Our dog is friendly.
He gave a friendly wave.

more.def: Kind and pleasant, and glad to be with other people.
examples: The friendly neighbor brought us cookies.
A friendly puppy wagged its tail at every visitor.
She was friendly to everyone on the first day of school.
Our friendship is strong.
I value our friendship.
Friendship is important.

more.def: The close, kind bond between friends.
examples: Their friendship began on the first day of school.
A good friendship is built on trust and sharing.
Our friendship has lasted many years.
Loud noises frighten my cat.
The big dog frightened the baby.
Spiders do not frighten me.

more.def: To make someone feel afraid.
examples: The sudden bang frightened the horses.
The scary movie frightened my little brother.
A sudden shadow frightened the fish away.
The kitten was frightened.
I felt frightened in the dark.
He was frightened by the loud noise.

more.def: Afraid or scared, often because of something sudden.
examples: The frightened rabbit hid in the bush.
She was frightened by the loud thunder.
The little boy felt frightened when the lights went out.

easy.def: A word that shows where something starts.
examples: I came from school.
This gift is from Grandma.
The bus is far from here.

more.def: A word used to show where something starts, or what it was made of.
examples: The train travels from the city to the mountains.
Maple syrup comes from the sap of maple trees.
Our school is open from eight in the morning until three.
Sit in the front of the car.
The front of the house is blue.
The teacher stands at the front of the class.

more.def: The side or part of something that faces forward or is seen first.
examples: The front of the card has a picture of a bear.
A bell hung on the front of the old bus.
Please come to the front of the room and read your poem.

easy.def: Facing forward or near the start.
examples: Knock on the front door.
She sat in the front seat.
We sat in the front row.

more.def: Located at the part of something that faces forward or is seen first.
examples: We painted the front door bright red.
The front page of the newspaper had a picture of the parade.
Students in the front row had the best view of the stage.

easy.def: A sweet food that grows on trees or plants, like an apple.
examples: I eat fruit for a snack.
An apple is a fruit.
The fruit is ripe.

more.def: The sweet part of a plant that holds seeds, such as an apple or a berry.
examples: Apples, bananas and peaches are all fruit.
Birds eat the fruit from the tree.
She put fresh fruit in her cereal.

easy.def: To cook food in hot oil.
examples: Mom will fry an egg.
We fried the fish.
Fry the potatoes.

more.def: To cook food in a pan with hot oil or butter.
examples: Dad fried eggs for breakfast.
Fry the onions until they are soft.
We fried the potatoes in a pan.
